Is the canonical height ĥf (P ) always in Q? If not, give necessary and sufficient conditions for ĥf (P ) ∈ Q. Question 16.14 is open, even for N = 1, but the following result for local canon- ical heights is known.
target_in_paper: Question 16.14 in Section 16 (Canonical Heights), with nearby motivating context from Theorem 16.8, Conjecture 16.9, Theorem 16.11, and the contrast provided by Theorem 16.15.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical core of Question 16.14 almost verbatim: it is about the dynamical canonical height over the function field K(B) of a curve, for a degree d >= 2 morphism f: P^N -> P^N defined over K(B), evaluated at a point P in P^N(K(B)); and it asks whether hat h_f(P) is always rational, or else for a characterization of when hat h_f(P) lies in Q. You also correctly reflect the paper's immediate context by noting that the problem remains open even for N = 1 and that only a local-height result is known nearby.
missing_details: The question should explicitly identify B as an algebraic curve over a field K, with K(B) its function field.

To be fully stand-alone, it should say that hat h_f is the dynamical (Call-Silverman) canonical height over the function field K(B), obtained from the usual function-field height by the limit hat h_f(P) = lim_{n->infty} d^{-n} h(f^n(P)).
It should make clear that the scope is morphisms f: P^N -> P^N, not arbitrary rational self-maps.
It should keep the point hypothesis exactly as in the paper: P is K(B)-rational, i.e. P in P^N(K(B)).
The trailing sentence about local canonical heights is surrounding context from the paper, not part of the research question itself, so it should be separated from the final formulation.

If one wants the motivation to be paper-faithful, one should note that the question is posed after special cases where an associated divisor E_{f,P} is known to lie in Div(B) tensor Q, which forces rationality of the resulting global canonical height; this explains why the paper asks the general rationality question at this point.
The official formulation is global: it concerns the global canonical height hat h_f(P), not the local canonical heights lambda_{f,v}.
refined_question: Let B be an algebraic curve over a field K, let K(B) be its function field, let f: P^N -> P^N be a morphism of degree d >= 2 defined over K(B), and let P be a point of P^N(K(B)). If hat h_f denotes the dynamical canonical height over the function field K(B), equivalently hat h_f(P) = lim_{n->infty} d^{-n} h(f^n(P)) with h the usual function-field height on P^N(K(B)), must hat h_f(P) always lie in Q? If not, give necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair (f, P) for hat h_f(P) to be rational.
justification: The nearest official target is Question 16.14 itself, not the neighboring local-height theorem. The surrounding discussion first reinterprets algebraic families ft and sections P over a curve B as a single morphism f over the function field K(B) with a K(B)-point P, and recalls the function-field canonical height in that setting. Theorem 16.8 gives the asymptotic specialization formula, Tate's formula (16.5) and Conjecture 16.9 introduce the divisor E_{f,P}, and Theorem 16.11 proves in a large polynomial case that E_{f,P} actually lies in Div(B) tensor Q, which in turn yields rationality of the global canonical height. Question 16.14 is then posed as the general rationality problem. Theorem 16.15 immediately after it concerns irrational local canonical heights for rational maps on P^1 and is included only to show that a local argument will not settle the global question.
